payload.claim: `_first_kept_line_after` assumes `end` (the offset right after `find`) always falls at a line boundary. When `find` is a sub-line fragment rather than a whole line (plausible for a wrong-version or criterion-probe edit that targets one keyword, as the motivating `risk=` example itself describes), `before[end:]` begins mid-line, so the first `split("\n")` chunk is the tail of `find`'s own line, not a genuine following line. `_indent()` is then computed on that tail, which has no real leading indentation, so the adoption guard at lines 267-269 under-measures indentation and can fail to refuse an edit whose added block actually swallows a subsequent kept line as its body. `_kept_line_at` (lines 183-188) avoids this by re-deriving the true line start with `rfind`; `_first_kept_line_after` has no equivalent safeguard, and no test in this change exercises a `find` that ends mid-line, so the gap is invisible to the gates.
